title: «Χάπι βιασμού»: Νέα εξέταση επιτρέπει την ανίχνευση της ουσίας έως και 48 ώρες μετά τη χρήση
excerpt: Με τη νέα μέθοδο, τα θύματα θα έχουν περισσότερες δυνατότητες να δικαιωθούν. Τι επισημαίνει στο iatropedia.gr η Δρ. Χρ. Σαρδέλη, Καθηγήτρια Φαρμακολογίας ΑΠΘ
summary: Μια σημαντική επιστημονική εξέλιξη στον εντοπισμό της ουσίας GHB, γνωστή και ως «χάπι του βιασμού», έρχεται από τη Δανία. Ερευνητές του Πανεπιστημίου του Άαρχους ανακάλυψαν ένα μόριο που μπορεί να λειτουργήσει ως βιοδείκτης της συγκεκριμένης ουσίας, επιτρέποντας την ανίχνευση της κατανάλωσής της έως και 48 ώρες μετά τη λήψη της. Η ανακάλυψη αυτή θεωρείται ιδιαίτερα σημαντική, καθώς μέχρι σήμερα ο εντοπισμός του GHB αποτελούσε μια σοβαρή πρόκληση για τις ιατροδικαστικές αρχές. Ο λόγος; Η ουσία αποβάλλεται γρήγορα από τον οργανισμό, με αποτέλεσμα το χρονικό περιθώριο ανίχνευσής της να είναι εξαιρετικά περιορισμένο, από 12 έως 18 ώρες.

title: Researchers Just Figured Out a Way to Detect Ovarian Cancer Earlier Than Ever
excerpt: This could be life-saving.
summary: More than 21,000 women in the U.S. are diagnosed with ovarian cancer each year. While it’s not the most common cancer in women, ovarian cancer is considered the deadliest cancer in women worldwide because it’s often diagnosed at later stages, has a high rate of recurrence, and is difficult to treat. Right now, the five-year survival rate of ovarian cancer is just 52 percent. As with most cancers, detecting the disease early may increase the odds of survival. Researchers recently discovered a new way to detect earlier stages of the cancer, potentially helping thousands of women.

excerpt: A new study shows a strong link.
summary: Temperatures are starting to rise, with some parts of the US facing a record-setting early heat wave this week. But while you’re probably focused on staying cool, there’s one more thing that should be on your radar: a higher-than-usual risk of migraine headaches. That’s the major takeaway from new research published in the journal Neurology: The study uncovered three lesser-known factors that can trigger migraine—and these triggers can crop up even more in the late spring and summer.

title: How to Have Great Sex After 60, According to Experts
excerpt: “I had my first real orgasm—that I didn’t have to fake—at 61.”
summary: There’s a common assumption that great, adventurous sex is a young person’s game—and with age, it fades into something boring, nonexistent, or just…not worth the effort. Growing up, Karen Bigman fell for the propaganda. “But recently, I’ve done it in restaurant bathrooms,” Bigman, a 62-year-old certified sex educator, tells SELF, before listing off other examples of her scandalous escapades. “I’ve spontaneously met up in hotel rooms when the kids were at home. We even pulled over next to a Duane Reade, under the fluorescent lamp, to do it in the back seat of his car.”

title: Incline Walking vs. Running: What’s the Better Workout?
excerpt: The answer depends on your goals, fitness level, and how hard you're ready to push your body.
summary: Incline walking and running are commonly framed as opposites: one is low impact, the other is high-intensity. But in reality, they’re both effective cardio options that challenge your body in distinct ways—from the muscles you recruit to the impact on your joints. Both workouts can boost your heart health, build endurance, and leave you seriously sweaty, but they place different demands on your body, according to Gab Reznik, CPT and Tone House coach. The question isn’t which is better across the board—it’s which is better for you depending on your goals.

title: Having ‘Boring’ Conversations Is Really Good for You, Psychologists Say
excerpt: They can have a big impact on your health.
summary: It’s tempting to try to bypass coworkers in the break room or limit small talk with the person waiting next to you in an effort to avoid what you suspect will be a dull conversation. But new research makes a solid argument for leaning into these “boring” chats. The study, which was published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, found that people who actually engage in these conversations thought that they were much more interesting and enjoyable than they expected. But beyond that, there is data to suggest that having these “boring” conversations could do your mental and physical health a solid.

title: Meet the WNBA's Next Class of Rookies
excerpt: From draft night to rookie season goals, the 2026 class is entering the league at a major turning point.
summary: The newest class of the WNBA is already stepping into the spotlight. Monday’s draft night delivered all the energy you’d expect from a league entering a pivotal chapter. With a new collective bargaining agreement reshaping conversations around players’ salaries, benefits, and long-term investment, the future of the WNBA is looking bigger, better, and brighter. This year’s top picks come in with stacked resumes, impressive tournament runs, championship wins, and star power already on the rise. Draft night may be over, but the real story is just getting started.

title: Everyone Wants This Unapproved Weight Loss Drug—And Some Have Found a Way to Get It
excerpt: Retatrutide is hailed as a game changer, but experts caution against taking any medication that is still being tested.
summary: For all the hype surrounding GLP-1 weight loss medications like Wegovy and Zepbound, these drugs don’t work for everyone. Nearly 17% of people on these medications are considered “non-responders,” leaving them looking for a different solution. But there’s a buzzy new medication waiting in the wings. While it’s not yet approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), people are already seeking it out. It’s called retatrutide, and it’s a triple-agonist medication, which means it acts on three different receptors in the body. By comparison, Wegovy (semaglutide) acts on one receptor, while Zepbound (tirzepatide) works on two.

title: Why Are People Taking CoQ10 Supplements for Longevity, and Do They Work?
excerpt: The antioxidant is trending because of how it supports our cells’ critical energy-makers, mitochondria.
summary: Coenzyme Q10, or CoQ10, was once a niche supplement, known best in wellness circles for its possible benefits for heart health and fertility. But now the antioxidant’s star is rising for a new reason: its purported longevity-boosting powers. The appeal of CoQ10 has grown as researchers have explored its effects on various conditions, with small studies revealing, for example, it may help boost insulin sensitivity, cut the frequency of migraine attacks, and alleviate muscle aches from statins used for high cholesterol.

title: What Is ‘Fiber Training’—And Why Should You Be Doing It?
excerpt: Slow and steady wins the race.
summary: With the fibermaxxing fad encouraging people to prioritize this chronically neglected nutrient, one issue keeps coming up: the side effects. As important as hitting your daily fiber goal is, your body doesn’t always make doing so easy. Fiber is difficult for your digestive system to break down and has to be handed off to bacteria in the colon instead (which is kind of its point), so piling on too much too fast can result in a barrage of painful, awkward, or inconvenient digestive symptoms—bloating, gas, stomach cramps, the whole nine yards.

title: Yes, Your Feet Age. Dermal Fillers Can Help
excerpt: The common aesthetic treatment might revive the pep in your step.
summary: Barefoot walks on the beach. A day in their favorite high heels. A long training walk ahead of the Camano de Santiago. These are the goals—big and small—of women undergoing foot filler treatments. Using an injectable filler—such as hyaluronic acid or body fat—to add padding to sore feet is not new, though it is gaining in popularity. As early as the 1960s, medical-grade silicone has been used to puff up padding deflated by age, years of wear and tear, and fashionable footwear, especially high heels. All of this puts intense pressure on the balls of the feet—otherwise known as the metatarsals.

title: 5 Signs You’re in a One-Sided Friendship, According to Experts
excerpt: Always reaching out first? It might be more than just bad timing.
summary: Welcome to Asking for a Friend, a weekly series dedicated to solving the messy, awkward, and confusing parts of modern friendship. Because truth is, our platonic relationships are often the most complicated. Send us your friendship dilemmas here, and we might feature one in a future column. Most friendships will never be truly 50/50, but at the very least they run on an unspoken agreement: both people show up, reach out, and add some fuel to the tank that keeps the engine going. If that balance consistently feels off—not just once or twice, but over the course of weeks or months—it’s hard not to wonder whether something deeper is going on.

title: Are Single Older Ladies Really Happy Without Marriage? Experts Weigh In
excerpt: Once seen as a last resort, life without a husband is gaining new appeal.
summary: At some point in most women’s lives, a familiar line of thinking creeps in—whether on its own or planted by well-meaning parents: What if I don’t get married? What if I never find my person and end up alone? For Joan, the panic hit in her 30s—strong enough to land her in a psychologist’s office.

title: 6 Supplements Doctors Actually Take
excerpt: Physicians say they can fill in nutritional gaps when necessary, but there are some caveats.
summary: These days, it seems like everyone is taking a supplement—to look better, think better, sleep better, relax better, poop better, or work out better. And you’re not imagining things: Half of adults and one-third of children in the United States take supplements regularly, according to the Office of Dietary Supplements. Supplements may be ubiquitous, but many experts have serious reservations about their rise. First, most physicians recommend obtaining nutrients directly from food rather than a pill or capsule. Second, supplements aren’t reviewed for safety and effectiveness by the FDA before they hit shelves.

title: What Is ‘Nonnamaxxing’? The Italian Grandma Lifestyle Might Be the Secret to Longevity
excerpt: For a happier and healthier life, try these sensible habits.
summary: When I moved to Italy in 2024, one of the first things I noticed was the very particular way Italian nonne, or grandmas, live. They walk everywhere, frequently across the city, without any assistance. Many of them are dressed to the nines, but they also don’t try to hide their age. I was then delighted—and unsurprised—when I came across a new wellness trend making the rounds on social media. “Nonnamaxxing” is the idea that anyone can maximize their life if they just embrace the habits of Italian grandmas. It happens to be sensible guidance.

title: Are GLP-1 Drugs Quietly Changing Our Sex Lives?
excerpt: Here’s everything we know so far.
summary: By now you’ve probably heard about GLP-1s, sold under brand names such as Ozempic and Wegovy. This class of medications mimics naturally occurring hormones involved in appetite control and blood sugar regulation to treat type 2 diabetes and aid weight-loss efforts. It should be no surprise, then, that conversations around these popular drugs have largely centered on the scale. However, some scientists are starting to look more closely into how they may impact something perhaps even more personal: our sex lives.
